findings.claim: The review-panel `manifest` operation never reads an existing manifest.json and takes the panel size from `--lenses` or the 3-lens default, so re-running `manifest` on a run whose manifest already records a different lens count silently rewrites the manifest to the new (smaller) size and exits 0; the subsequent `tally` then adjudicates only the surviving prefix lenses' verdict files with a lower strict-majority floor, wrongly refutes findings the full panel upheld, and promotes the task blocked → passed.

evidence.setup: Snapshot 8ce7c58 CLI driven for real (bun engine/src/cli.ts helper review-panel ...) in a temp fixture: one wave-1 task T1, review_status "blocked", one critical finding (id T1:code-reviewer-1, file src/x.ts). Steps: brief --wave 1 (exit 0) → manifest --lenses 5 (exit 0; manifest.json records lenses [reproduction, intent, blast-radius, security, test-coverage]) → five verdict files written via `verdict --lens <lens>` into verdicts/verdict-N.json in manifest lens order: slot 1 refuted, slot 2 refuted, slots 3-5 upheld.
evidence.input: Retry of runbook Step 3.5.2: `helper review-panel manifest --runs-root .claude/reviews/panel-runs --run-dir <run>` with NO --lenses, then `helper review-panel tally --runs-root .claude/reviews/panel-runs --manifest <run>/manifest.json`.
evidence.observed: Manifest re-run: exit 0, manifest.json now records [reproduction, intent, blast-radius]. Second tally: exit 0, stderr "Refutation panel: 0 finding(s) survived, 1 refuted (3 lenses, threshold 2)", the finding moved into the task's refuted_findings and the task's review_status became "passed"; verdict-4.json and verdict-5.json remain on disk, never opened (readVerdicts iterates only the shrunken lens list). The identical first tally on the 5-lens manifest had correctly reported "1 finding(s) survived, 0 refuted (5 lenses, threshold 3)" and left the task blocked.
evidence.expected: The panel size is fixed for the life of the run: the manifest records it and every later operation recovers it from the file (wave-gate.md Step 3.5.2; the module's own lens-selection comment). A `manifest` re-run must either agree with the recorded count or be rejected with a contract error, as the sibling `--threshold` guard at lines 352-363 refuses a bar below the strict majority — "a weaker panel must not run under the same name". With verdicts 1-2 refuting and 3-5 upholding, 2 < 3, the finding survives and the task stays blocked.
evidence.reference: engine/src/handlers/helpers/review-panel.ts lines 253-265 (manifestRaw deliberately left null on the write path, so manifestLensCount(manifestRaw) is null and lensCount falls back to REVIEW_LENSES_DEFAULT or to whatever the re-run passes in --lenses, with no comparison against the recorded count) and line 354 (floor computed from the shrunken manifest lens list); commands/wave-gate.md Step 3.5.2 ("Default panel size is 3. Pass --lenses N (2–5) to manifest ... The manifest records the size").

violatedContract.statement: The manifest is the sole finding-set and lens-set authority for all later stages of the run: it fixes the exact lens list before verifiers spawn, the panel size is recorded once, and `lenses`, `verdict`, and `tally` recover it from the file; the refutation threshold is a strict majority of the recorded panel and is a floor that may only be raised, never lowered. The operation that authors the manifest must not silently re-size a panel whose verdicts were cast by the recorded one.

consequence.affected: The wave gate's refutation adjudication and the task graph state it writes: a critical finding the full panel upheld is recorded as refuted (moved out of critical_findings into refuted_findings) and the task is promoted blocked → passed, unblocking a wave that the engine's own majority rule says must stay blocked.
consequence.preconditions: A review run whose manifest.json records a lens count different from the re-run's requested/default count (e.g. a documented `--lenses 4` or `--lenses 5` run — 2–5 is the documented supported range), followed by `manifest` being invoked again on the same run directory. The engine itself invites and supports such re-runs: prepareWriteTargets explicitly permits overwriting an existing manifest.json "in place", and the runbook sanctions re-executing steps after transient failures; the shrink is fully silent (exit 0, no stderr signal that the panel changed).
consequence.impact: readVerdicts then validates only the first N lenses' slots, silently ignores surplus verdict files that are positive evidence of the larger panel that actually ran, and tallyRefutations applies a strict-majority floor computed from the shrunken list (e.g. 2 of 3 instead of 3 of 5). The gate's authority decision is flipped at exit 0; the operator sees only "(3 lenses, threshold 2)", indistinguishable from a legitimately 3-lens run.
consequence.evidenceLimits: Reviewer-reported execution against the snapshot CLI, not an engine execution receipt. Directly observed: exit codes, the rewritten manifest.json content, the tally stderr lines, the verdict files left on disk, and the resulting task graph state. Not observed or proved: the downstream complete-wave-gate advancement of the wave, and whether an orchestrator strictly obeying the prose "Never reuse an existing run directory" would ever re-enter this path — the engine does not enforce that prose, and the engine's own write path (prepareWriteTargets overwrite-in-place) anticipates manifest re-runs.

basis.severityRationale: A silent, exit-0 weakening of the gate that decides whether a wave ships: exactly the 'weaker panel wearing the same name' the module's own threshold guard (lines 352-363) exists to refuse, applied to the panel size instead of the threshold, with a wrongly refuted critical and a blocked → passed promotion as the concrete consequence. Safe operator use (retrying a documented engine-authored step) must not be able to flip the gate; this blocks delivery.

findings.claim: Re-running `tally` on an already-tallied run lets the invariant Error thrown by applyFindingOutcomes escape the helper as an uncaught hook error with a misleading recovery hint, instead of reaching the operator as a contract diagnostic.
findings.reason: Reproduced against the snapshot: after a successful refuting tally (task passed, finding in refuted_findings), a second `tally` on the same run exits 1 with "Hook error: findings invariant: T1 has no finding 'code-reviewer-1' the panel adjudicated — the task graph changed between brief and tally; re-run the brief". The likelier cause is an operator re-run — invited, for example, by a failed canonical-output write that lands after the state write at lines 375-378 — and the hint is wrong: re-running `brief` rebuilds from the post-tally state, which can never reproduce the adjudicated finding set, so following it dead-ends the run. The state itself stays correct (atomicWrite computes the new state before writing, and the throw aborts before any write), and the gate remains fail-closed, so no wrong adjudication occurs. Catching the invariant error and reporting it as a "review tally" contract error that names the replay ("this run has already been tallied; start a new run directory") would reach the operator like every other failure in this helper. Nonblocking correction.

findings.claim: The flag-documentation check tests prose.includes(flag), so "--lens" is vacuously satisfied by the substring inside "--lenses"; the runbook could stop documenting the verdict step's required --lens flag without failing the binding this commit creates.
findings.reason: Substring containment cannot distinguish a flag from its longer neighbor, so the exact drift class this test exists to catch (a handler-read flag absent from the prose) survives for --lens. Matching flag occurrences as whole tokens (boundary-aware regex) would close the gap. Nonblocking: in the snapshot the runbook does document --lens at Step 3.5.3, so the assertion is true today; this is a robustness improvement to the new guard, not a present failure.

findings.claim: parseMachineSummary trims the Machine Summary section at ANY level-2..4 heading (its own comment says "same or higher level"), so a summary that sub-heads its findings section loses every marker line and the task is marked evidence_capture_failed.
findings.reason: Probe: "### Machine Summary" followed by "#### Critical Findings" and then CRITICAL_COUNT/CRITICAL: lines resolves to kind "evidence-failed" ("CRITICAL_COUNT marker not found"), while the same content without the sub-heading parses cleanly. Fail-closed and recoverable by re-spawning the reviewer, but it spuriously fails a well-formed review with a diagnostic that misattributes the cause to a missing marker; the comment also misdescribes the implemented rule. Fix by trimming only at headings of the summary's own level or higher.
